item: Three pinned nflverse mirrors (games, injuries_2026, snap_counts_2026) now carry a different asset digest upstream than the copy this desk reads.
detail: Local copies match the digest their owning session recorded on 2026-11-12T16:52:39Z, so the desk's inputs are internally consistent and reproducible. The upstream release has been republished since. Every number in this build is therefore correct *for the pin*, and would move if the pin moved.
action: Re-pin deliberately or accept the pin. Do not silently refresh.

item: The aggregator odds page splits an opening price across two team rows (open spread on the favourite's row, open total prefixed o/u on the other).
detail: Which row a number sits on appears to carry meaning the page never states. The open total is recorded as displayed with the prefix kept in raw_display and is excluded from every computed move statistic.
action: Two-sample comparison (question MK-Q-03). Until then: no line-move claims.

item: Four games show implausibly large open-to-current moves on a single page: MIA@IND 47.5 to 37.5 total, LAR@ARI 47.5 to 39.5, JAX@TEN -2.5 to -10.5 side, and IND@HOU -5.5 to -10.0 five days out.
detail: Either the market moved on news this desk cannot see, or the page's open column is not an open. Both readings are recorded, neither is resolved; the numbers are kept verbatim in the store and excluded from any movement claim.
action: Second-source confirmation before any of these four games is used as an example.

item: The standings page renders the Rams as 'LA' and the Cardinals as 'AZ'; the schedule pages and this desk's keys use LAR and ARI.
detail: Mapped explicitly in pinned/capture.py (STANDINGS_PAGE_ABBREV) so a transcription is not silently keyed to a different club. The mirror uses LA for the Rams in its own team column.
action: None needed - the mapping is the fix. Any new source must be added to the same map.

item: The prop rows were captured from a page whose tab titles were not in the rendered text; the tab identity is inferred from render order.
detail: Prop rows are therefore labelled as observations and never graded or used in a correlation - which is also why the prop division is blocked (MK-Q-05).
action: Re-capture with the tab label in the transcription, or drop prop rows from the store.

item: The official Week 10 injury report and the mirror's injury feed disagree on row counts for the same week: 326 vs 276.
detail: Official-only names include LAC Daiyan Henley, IND Grover Stewart, BAL Jaylinn Hawkins; the mirror adds rows the official page does not list on that date. Per-club counts are published in availability_source_diff.csv rather than reconciled by preference.
action: Answer MK-Q-04 before the availability base rate is quoted as a rate.

item: Two inputs were vendored from another session's files rather than fetched from the source by this session: the Week 10 official injury report and the 31-club depth-chart transcription.
detail: Both are pinned by digest in pinned/vendor_manifest.json, and every row in the derived tables carries the *original* official URL, so a reviewer can check the upstream page directly. What this session did not do is re-read those pages itself.
action: A reviewer spot-checks three rows against the live official page; the manifest digest then becomes a verified pin rather than a transcription claim.

item: The results feed carries an official URL for every 2026 game in the vendored slate, but the score field for 137 of them was verified against the pinned mirror rather than against 137 individually fetched official pages.
detail: Reading each game's own nfl.com page would be 137 fetches. The reconciliation is still three-way in effect (transcription vs mirror vs standings totals) and the standings reconciliation would fail loudly if any score were wrong - RF-02 checks W/L/T/PF/PA for all 32 clubs, which pins every score in aggregate.
action: Per-game official fetches in the CI job, one slate per run, until coverage reaches 100%.

item: The QB-vs-top-WR yards correlation (r=0.76) published by an earlier session is not reproduced in this desk's correlation table.
detail: It is computed from a third-party play-by-play dump, and requirement 7 restricts correlations to officially sourced numbers. The row is printed as NOT COMPUTED with that reason, so the absence is visible rather than looking like a zero.
action: Pin an official play-by-play asset (MK-Q-05) and the row becomes computable.

item: The Munich neutral-site marker for NE@DET came from the vendored transcription, not from an official page this session read.
detail: Resolved in-build: the pinned mirror marks the game 'Neutral' with stadium 'FC Bayern Munich Stadium', and check RF-13 now reconciles all nine 2026 international rows against that column, so no neutral-site claim in this build is unverified.
action: None - kept in the register so the origin of the claim stays visible.

item: No strategy clears the gates. The walk-forward model forecasts the margin at r=0.29 where the posted line forecasts it at r=0.45, and its total is worse still (r=0.055).
detail: This is not a build failure - it is the honest result of an honest test, and it is the reason nothing is promoted. The desk publishes a model that loses to the market rather than a model tuned until it wins.
action: Either improve the forecast (see suggestions MK-SG-02, MK-SG-08) or keep the desk paper-only. Tuning the gates until something passes is not an action.

item: data/live_bets.csv ships with a header and no rows.
detail: The demotion gate reads it, and the gate is therefore 'armed, not passed'. Populating it with plausible-looking bets to demonstrate the machinery would have been the one truly unforgivable fabrication in this build.
action: None. If a live strategy ever exists, the ledger fills and the gate evaluates.
